candidates.trace: validate_equipment checks each authored dimensions_m component as a finite positive f64, while EquipmentPhysical stores [f32; 3]. For a hypothetical 1e-100 component, the f64 predicate is true but IEEE-754 f32 narrowing yields zero. Under the pinned serde_json non-arbitrary-precision Value deserializer, the typed preflight dispatches the f64 to serde_core f32 visitor, which casts it without rejecting zero. validate_documents_with_sources checks only whether typed deserialization returned an error and discards the decoded value; compile_items serializes the original validated Value. This is a source-based conditional construction, not a run of the parser or validator. The separate positive_f32_in helper does check positivity after narrowing for its selected shield and surface callers, but the dimension check does not call it.
candidates.connected_path: The checked-in utility knife has explicit left- and right-hand placements and positive dimensions. As a hypothetical author change only, replacing its x component with 1e-100 leaves the inspected f64 dimension predicate satisfied. The catalogue loader later deserializes embedded JSON; its generated melee recipe replaces y length and grip, not x. The tactical projection copies the x component into TacticalEquipmentPhysical even when instance geometry changes y. If runtime decoding produces x == 0 and such an item is in a hand with no children, TacticalEquipmentPhysical::is_valid is false and the selected drop path returns false before collider creation; the selected pickup path also filters invalid physical data. Other admission gates, item projection, actual supported setup and the decoder feature graph have not been executed or established.
